text:
The interesting part of AI right now isn't just better models.

It's what developers are building around them.
A model can generate code, but the real product needs repository context, tools, permissions and verification.
A model can answer questions, but a useful system needs retrieval, citations, evaluation and fresh data.
A model can call tools, but production needs state, retries, observability and security.

The model is becoming a component. The system around it is becoming the product. That shift creates a much bigger engineering surface,
context → tools → orchestration → inference → evaluation → observability → security

This is why AI engineering is starting to look a lot like systems engineering.
And that’s probably one of the most important shifts for developers to understand.

text:
«“It’s a system with gigantic memory and retrieval ability, not one that can invent solutions to new problems.”»
Von Neumann was a system with gigantic memory and retrieval. Somehow that's a frequent mark of creative genius in humans.
I think the core intuition one needs to respect LLMs is very basic. They are shapes, not code or mechanics. Weights describe the shape of the representation of the mind. The data – rather, the training signal – defines this shape, but we explicitly don't have facts in there, they get recomputed on the fly. Even engram-style memory modules contain no strings. This is, in fact, regrettably wasteful, but it's also why the relation of LLMs to data is not quite as hopelessly slavish as Yann imagines. They can and do find solutions to new problems. It's a bit too late to play these games.

author: GOATNetwork
quoted_text:
Every thesis I hold about the agent economy starts from this premise: unlike humans, agents don't have habits or predilections. They have raw objectives.

My Ekubo thesis applies that to trading. Agents will do most of our trading, and they'll route through the most capital-efficient infrastructure every time, because nothing else registers.

The same premise can be applied to saving.

An agent that earns capital has to store it somewhere, but freezable, reversible rails won't be acceptable to agents. They're disqualifying.

A @BitcoinPolicy Institute study of 9,000+ scenarios has already found that AI models converge on Bitcoin when they're left to do their own reasoning about storing value. Bitcoin took 79% of store-of-value responses, the strongest consensus in the entire study. Agents always look to optimize, and my thesis is that they will choose to hold it on a network where they can put it to work, and where exit back to Bitcoin is guaranteed by cryptography instead of any central operator.

Yield on @GOATNetwork is built into the network mechanics, so deploying that BTC isn't a decision. It's arithmetic.

So where does GOATED fit into this? It's the lever on that yield. Staking GOATED is what boosts the BTC returns, which means an agent optimizing the yield on its Bitcoin treats it as an input, the token that raises the return on the asset it already holds.

That's a very different adoption path from a token that needs believers. The math just has to be legible, which means an agent stakes GOATED when the boosted-minus-base yield on its BTC beats the cost of acquiring and holding GOATED.

The agent capital flywheel: earn, store value in Bitcoin, put it to work through GOATED, all on rails the agent deems most secure.

I think the core reason behind $IMD rise this time is not simply the AI Narrative, but that after POOL4 officially went live, the Token and the product’s economic mechanism finally became genuinely connected.

0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7

Previously, the market’s main bets on IMD were Identity.md, AI Agents, Autonomous Work, and the Uniswap v4 Hook. Now there is an additional and much clearer economic loop:

IMD Trading → POOL4 → Trim → 85% Burn + Staking / Bonding / NFT Node → Buy Wall

After POOL4 went live, Staking also launched. Around 560K IMD was staked within a short period of time, while Burn and reward distribution also began. This is the most direct catalyst for the sudden rise this time. The market has started to reprice IMD, rather than simply speculating on the AI concept.

More importantly, IMD’s fundamentals have genuinely changed.

Before:AI Agent → Narrative → Attention → IMD

Now:AI Agent → Autonomous Work → IMD → POOL4 → Trading → Burn / Staking → Bonding → Compute → Agent Economy

Bonding is one of the most important upcoming milestones. The official design is that Bonding will open when IMD reaches $4, and the Bonding Reserve can eventually be converted into ETH to pay for AI Inference. In other words, this could eventually form:

IMD → Bonding → ETH → AI Compute → Agent Work → Economic Activity → IMD

So what the market is really betting on now is not simply that “IMD is an AI Token,” but whether IMD can become the core asset of the AI Agent Economy + POOL4 economic mechanism.

POOL4 is also an important potential valuation expansion point. IMD is the first Token to use the POOL4 Hook. If other projects begin using POOL4 in the future and generate real trading volume, IMD’s positioning could evolve from an AI Agent Token into the representative native asset of POOL4.

The key upside catalysts to watch next are:

1. Bonding officially goes live
The Reserve becomes actual AI Compute demand, further strengthening Token Utility.

2. Agent numbers and real Work continue to grow
What matters is not simply the number of Agents, but whether Jobs, Accepted Work, and Compute continue increasing.

3. NFT Nodes go live
Part of the current Trim goes into the NFT Node Reserve. If the Node Economy officially launches, it will further expand IMD’s use cases.

4. A second successful POOL4 project emerges
If other Tokens use POOL4 and generate significant trading volume, the market may start assigning IMD an “Infrastructure / First Asset Premium.”

5. Volume → Burn continues to expand
If trading volume continues to grow while Burn, Staking, and Buy Walls also increase, the Token’s economic loop will truly begin to be validated.

At the moment, I believe IMD’s fundamentals have strengthened rather than weakened. But it is currently at:

Narrative Validated → Product Live → Economic Mechanism Live → Waiting for Scale Validation

The biggest issue is also very clear:Mechanism going live ≠ Mechanism succeeding.

If we see:Volume ↑ → Burn ↑ → Agent Work ↑ → Bonding ↑ → Compute ↑

then this rise can gradually transition from “expectation-driven trading” into “fundamental expansion.”

On the other hand, if the price continues rising while Volume, Burn, Agent Work, and Bonding do not grow alongside it, then this move will increasingly depend on Narrative and expectations, and the risk will also increase significantly.

So, in summary:The direct catalysts for this rise are the launch of POOL4 + Staking. The real long-term bet is whether IMD can evolve from an AI Agent Token into the core economic asset of the AI Agent Economy + POOL4.

"You shouldn't invest the money you have. You should invest the money you're ever going to have." An ex-IMC trader on why young people are under-allocated:

Lihong Wang (@Lihong062), traded semiconductor options at IMC, one of the largest options market makers in the world.

Lihong explains:

"People discuss rising inequality in the US, driven by rising asset prices. There are moral statements you can make about this, but that trend is probably going to continue. If you truly believe AI is gonna create value, more value is gonna accrue to capital."

"If you're really young, 18, 20, 22, you're not married, no kids, no real responsibilities, there's no particular reason you shouldn't be at least a little bit leveraged. And this is not financial advice, for legal purposes."

"Consider how much the average college kid has in savings by senior year. A few hundred, few thousand dollars. Then consider how much they'll have after working a few years. As your career progresses and your human capital compounds, you're gonna make exponentially more."

"Which means super early on, most people are extremely under-allocated into capital. You shouldn't really just invest how much money you have right now. You should, in some sense, invest how much money you're ever going to have."

"This is made really clear in trading. Kids get offers between 600K to a million a year, and they're starting with a 50 to 100K portfolio from internship money. By the end of the year they're guaranteed to at least 4, 5x that. There's no reason they shouldn't be 3 to 4x leveraged."

Wrapped-up a very productive week in New York alongside UNGA 2026. A few highlights:

Participated at a business roundtable: "Africa Forward—Investing in the Next Decade of Growth,". High-level speakers included Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele of Nigeria. Roundtable discussions led by Flutterwave’s co-founder and CEO, Olugbenga "GB" Agboola.

Joined panel discussions on financing Africa's future at Standard Charter Bank’s New York headquarters, with a keynote by President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah of Namibia. 

Attended a critical minerals forum at the St. Regis Hotel, with featured speakers including President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of Somalia and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo.

Had a great networking opportunity at a business reception hosted by Invest Africa and Concerto. The room was full of sharp minds from tech, mining, investment banking and beyond, and the conversations were excellent.

Why these annual NY gatherings matter: UNGA week has become far more than a diplomatic gathering. With heads of state, finance ministers, global banks, investors and entrepreneurs all in one city, it is now one of the most important marketplaces for shaping Africa's economic future.

The conversations this year reflected a clear shift. Africa is no longer discussed mainly through the lens of aid, but as a destination for long-term capital. Critical minerals place the continent at the center of the global energy transition. Fintech and digital payments are expanding access at remarkable speed. And with the world's youngest and fastest-growing population, Africa's demand for infrastructure, housing, energy and financial services represents one of the largest investment opportunities of the coming decades.

The task now is to turn these conversations into deals: deepening local capital markets, mobilizing domestic and international financing together, and p the global stage.

币圈有时候会出现一些特别的事件，让所有人提前很久就知道它哪天发生，但真到了那一天，市场依旧还是会盯得死死的。

Token Unlock 就是这样。
9月25日，XPL迎来一次大规模解锁，金额约1.53亿美元，相当于当前已解锁供应量的63.2%。
而且这次比较特殊：Private Investors、Founder/Team 等份额开始进入可转让阶段。

这么大的供应出来，市场不是早就知道了吗？
对，但是知道，和已经消化，是两回事。

Token Unlock不像黑天鹅。
黑天鹅的问题是没人知道它什么时候来；Unlock反过来，它甚至把闹钟提前给你定好了。

但市场真正不知道的是：拿到Token的人会不会卖？多少人准备提前对冲？多少资金已经提前撤退？释放出来的Token会立刻进入市场，还是继续持有？市场深度能不能接住……

所以同样一个“解锁1亿美元”，放到不同项目、不同流动性环境、不同持有人结构里，结果完全可能不一样。

而这次XPL解锁也不是一次性结束。剩余的团队和投资者份额，还将继续按月释放至2028年9月。

价格真正交易的，并不只是“供应增加”这件事，而是所有人对供应增加之后会发生什么的预期。

所有人都知道闹钟几点响，有人提前一个小时起床，有人戴上耳塞继续睡，还有人专门坐在床边等它响。

只是闹钟响起来以后，房间里的人会干什么呢。

text:
How to grow on X if you're stuck at 500–1K followers ↓

1. Networking is your meat.

You need to build coalitions and engagement groups.
Yeah, it sucks. No one loves to DM random people. But without this, you’ll grow at a very low speed.

See it like this:
Each person you cross-support is a new audience.
It’s a win-win: you get the audience of your new friend – and he gets yours.

Two rules:

a. It has to be fair (no 10K account will be interested in cross-support with a 1K account), so don’t waste time DMing big accounts asking for help.

b. It has to be ever-evolving. People tend to support 3–4 posts and then disappear. It’s normal. You have to run a continuous cycle of networking and onboard 2–3 new engagement friends per week.

2. Networking gives you visibility, but your content still has to do the conversion work.

1–2 great posts per week is enough.

But they need to be great. Not written by ChatGPT with zero original input. Otherwise, you’ll lose the attention of people from your friend’s community while he efficiently vampires yours (he’s a smart guy; he knows what people love reading).

Those 1–2 great posts are your anchor pieces. Build around them (summaries / self QTs / sharing with your engagement circle / posting on Reddit and LinkedIn).

Anchor → Distribution.

Same as in all GTM strategies.

text:
Anthropic cut the cost of a full binder design campaign from up to $10,000 per target in GPU spend to close to $150, and cut the hardware requirement for modeling large complexes from a multi-node cluster to a single GPU node.

That cost decided who could even attempt this kind of modeling. A lab without cluster access or six figures in compute budget stayed out of this work entirely, regardless of how good their biology was.

Triangle attention and triangle multiplication are what made structure prediction expensive in the first place, cubic in both time and memory.

> FlashPairformer's kernels cut that cost directly, beating the field standard by roughly 2.7 to 2.9x on triangle attention and 1.7 to 3.2x on triangle multiplication, reaching close to 4x end to end once stacked into a full model run.

> Speed alone still left large complexes out of reach. A separate low-memory mode is what let a single GPU node hold systems past 10,000 tokens, complexes like the ribosome and mitochondrial complex I that previously needed a multi-node cluster just to fit in memory.

A cheaper GPU run still stops short of the part of a binder design that actually gets tested.

Whether the resulting binder actually binds anything is answered in a wet lab rather than in a compute log, and @AnthropicAI pairs its own cheaper compute with exactly that through the @adaptyvbio competition, testing over 5,000 designs instead of stopping at the computational result.

Compute got cheap.

The wet lab is still the only place that gets to say yes.

Ah yes, excellent points. We shouldn't worry about AI risk, because remember, your ancestors were ravaged by tiger attacks, bubonic plague, smallpox, famine, earthquakes, and the Nazis. 

Thankfully there was always someone with a name like BoneGPT to stand up in the back and shout "STOP WORRYING ABOUT IT, ACCELERATE," and that's why we're here today.

It definitely wasn't because people banded together and SOLVED these problems by inventing vaccines, building sewers, forming alliances, and studying the earth.

You're naming problems that humankind has worked desperately over millennia to solve, as though it's evidence that problems just solve themselves. For none of these things did we say FUCK IT, IT'LL PROBABLY BE FINE IF WE DO LITERALLY NOTHING. It's the opposite: these are all stories about generations who fought valiantly to eliminate risks so that we, their successors, could live without them.

It's on us now to do the same. There WERE people at the time who for each of these things said, fuck it, God will save us.

Those people are not our ancestors. Our ancestors were the ones who got their shit together, solved these problems, and survived.

AI doesn't became safe on its own. We have to actually SOLVE safety and learn how to control these things.

And we will. It took enormous work to make sure planes don't fall out of the sky, or that space shuttles don't spontaneously combust, but we got there.

But we have to actually do it. We don't get to just talk about it.

We are going to willingly give control of almost all of the levers of society to AIs pretty soon. So we better be absolutely fucking sure that when we do, we're still in charge.

text:
就想买一点 Robinhood 链上的币，有必要这么折腾吗？

钱还在交易所，要先提出来，再看看怎么跨链、准备多少 Gas。单看每一步都不难，凑在一起就有点劝退了。

尤其只是小额买一笔的时候，除了币价还得算上这些费用。还没下单，先琢磨半天到底值不值。

所以 OKX CeDeFi 这次让我比较在意的就一点：能少折腾几步。

像 CashCat、Pons 这些 Robinhood 链上的币，可以直接用 OKX 交易所里的余额买，不用自己再提币、跨链、另外准备 Gas。首次使用按 App 提示开通，还是会涉及钱包，只是不用另外装一个、自己来回操作。

对我来说这个方便是实在的：不用为了买一点币，先把钱搬来搬去。省下来的时间，还不如多看看合约对不对、流动性怎么样。

至于限时 Gas 补贴，有当然好，但我还是会点开订单，看看实际扣多少、最后能拿到多少币。免 Gas 不等于这笔交易就便宜，更不代表值得买。要是因为少了点费用，就忍不住多做几笔，那也未必省到钱。

另一个我会留意的，是限价单。

有时候看上一个币，但觉得现在贵了点，又怕自己一刷到上涨就手痒。这种时候，如果交易页面支持限价，我更愿意挂一个自己能接受的价格，等不到就算了。总比隔几分钟打开看一眼，最后把原本的计划看没了强。

已经买了也一样。先想清楚涨到哪里愿意卖、亏到什么程度不想再扛，再看看能不能设好止盈止损。不过设了也不能完全撒手不管，波动太大或者流动性不够，实际成交价还是可能和预想的不一样。

想找币的话，可以复制合约地址到 OKX 搜索框，或从「交易 → 链上」进去。名字一样的不一定是同一个币，链和合约得先核对，再看报价和费用。

我觉得这类功能的用处，就是让本来就有的交易计划少一点麻烦。至于要不要买、买多少，还是得自己想清楚，不能因为下单方便了，手也跟着松了。

Gas 补贴是否有效、支持币种和订单功能，以所在地区 App 页面为准。

text:
i made +$300k trading memes in a month

here are 2 simple things that 90% of people don’t understand, and they’re what separates winners from losers:

1: the main thing you need to understand is that memes are basically leveraged beta on $BTC

if $BTC goes down to $60k - which is obviously possible - that’s roughly a 27% drop for BTC

But your meme portfolio could easily be down 60% from that

but if we keep trading around $80k for another month, or especially if we go higher, memes will probably keep running day after day

so if the market stays flat for another month, you would realistically make 2-3x

if the market goes higher and you actually hold your bags instead of selling early, 10x+ outcomes are absolutely possible

now ask yourself

what’s the probability we stay sideways for another month?

what’s the probability we dump before that?

and what’s the probability we go higher?

then calculate the risk/reward instead of just blindly buying

for example, i’d personally put it roughly like this

• 25% chance we stay sideways for more than a month
• 40% chance we go higher without a major pullback first
• 60% chance we eventually go lower

these probabilities overlap, because we could stay sideways for a month and still dump later

so for a simple one-month model, you could treat it as roughly

• 25% sideways
• 40% up
• 35% dump within the month

now assume memes do +150% in the sideways scenario, +900% in the bullish scenario, and -60% in the bearish scenario

the expected return would be:

0.25 × 150% + 0.40 × 900% - 0.35 × 60% = +376.5%

obviously that number looks insane because the entire setup is extremely asymmetric

your downside might be -60%, while the upside can be several hundred percent or even 10x if you catch the right coins

but it also shows how sensitive the whole calculation is to your assumptions

if your “10x” scenario is actually only 2x, the math changes completely

this is how you can think about whether trading any asset makes sense at any stage of the market

estimate the possible outcomes

estimate their probabilities

then compare expected upside to expected downside

the reason i’m saying all of this is because you can absolutely lose everything trading memes

so size accordingly and understand the risk you’re taking

and there’s one more thing i want to add because i think a lot of people are still in disbelief about this entire asset class

2: in a sense, every coin - even $BTC - is a community coin

there’s a community that collectively decided it has value based on something, and the market keeps trying to price that belief

memes work the same way

traders give them value based on something too

they don’t have revenue, so most of their value comes from collective belief, attention, identity, distribution, and the strength of the community behind them

take $ANSEM for example

if you believe ansem keeps pushing $ANSEM, ask yourself how high the mcap could realistically go at peak attention

• he has 1.4m followers
• look at how the market currently views him
• think about whether that perception gets stronger or weaker
• then ask yourself what the probability is that he simply stops caring about the coin

and compare that setup with alternatives

for example $USELESS, which i’d also describe as a kind of identity coin around unipcs

understand what exactly you’re trading when you buy a specific meme

once you understand that, you’ll start making much better decisions

@reserveprotocol is voting to set the opening position of its new Burn Gauge, a five-way dial ranging from burning 4 treasury $RSR for every 1 the protocol burns, to unlocking 4.

Holders adopted the gauge on September 17th. It only acts when platform fees on mints and total value locked market-buy RSR and burn it: "Nothing unlocks unless that burn is happening."

Voters rank all five settings by preference, lowest eliminated until one has a majority. Ballots stay encrypted until close, so no setting can be read as leading.

text:
Shielded Bitcoin vs Zcash:

Shielded Bitcoin is pretty clever tech given the constraints, but there’s a big gap that Zcash provides.

- Zcash: zk-proof of shielded transaction is validated by the miner at block inclusion. Invalid proofs are not included in the block, therefore you know any proof onchain is valid.

- Shielded Bitcoin: zk-proof is just stored on Bitcoin without checking for validity. A separate network is needed to determine if the proofs are valid and reconstruct the Sheilded transaction state. You can’t use the Shielded pool with Bitcoin Consensus alone, very much how most L2s function. Interestingly, this seems to be a massive technical improvement over the Lightning Network!

Am unclear on how or why the secondary network would function without PoW rewards.

An important detail is left to research, which is how the lock/unlock of L1 transparent BTC will work in practice. Look forward to seeing what they find here.

@Uniswap approved extending protocol fees and $UNI burns to @arc, @circle's Layer 1 live since September 16th, and rotating @gauntlet_xyz's emergency keys on the DAO-owned @Morpho vaults behind Uniswap Earn.

Arc would be the twelfth chain beyond Ethereum mainnet with fees on. Searchers claim Arc fees by paying a bridged, synthetic UNI, which is burned and matched by a burn of canonical UNI on Ethereum through @wormhole's bridge.

Registering a chain with that bridge was permissionless on Polygon and BNB Chain, but not anymore. "Those contracts now exist and are governance owned, so registering a new chain against them requires an onchain vote," Uniswap Labs wrote.

L2BEAT voted For, citing its support for earlier fee expansions, and plans to have its research team review the final executable at the onchain stage.

The second vote swaps three Sentinel addresses after Gauntlet upgraded its signing setup. A Sentinel is an emergency brake that can lower caps or undo a pending curator action, but cannot drain a vault. Depositors don't need to act.

382 wallets cast 20.2M UNI on Arc: 100.0% For, quorum cleared at 202.2%. An onchain vote follows.

383 wallets cast 18.2M UNI on the Sentinel rotation: 100.0% For, quorum cleared at 182.2%. Timelock execution is expected in early October.

两天前我写 $LEAF / CRC-20 的时候，重点其实不是预测它能涨多少。

我当时更关心的是几个验证点：

— Mint 结束之后有没有真实交易和流动性
— Market / Swap / LP 能不能逐步跑出来
— 最后它是一次性的 Bitcoin Native 实验，还是会形成一套新的资产发行范式

今天回来更新一下。

至少第一个阶段，已经开始明显兑现了。🌱

截至 Bitcoin block 968,544：

441 Transfers

157 个今日活跃地址
今日约 80.77M LEAF moved
累计约 198.51M LEAF moved

几天前大家讨论的核心还是「怎么 Mint」。

现在已经开始进入「Mint 出来的资产能不能真正流转和交易」这个阶段。

所以我暂时不会拿某一个网页报价直接算市值，更不会因为现在开始有人晒几十倍，就把它变成一条“赶紧追”的 Call。

我自己是前面实际参与了 LEAF 的，不是今天涨了以后才开始研究。

现在我更关心：

二级市场到底能承载多少真实卖盘？
Swap / LP 和持续流动性能不能形成？
CRC-20 后面能不能跑出第二、第三个有生命力的资产？

author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
最近参与并研究了一个挺有意思的 Bitcoin Native 早期实验：$LEAF / CRC-20。

先留个时间戳。

简单来说，CRC-20 / PRECOP 想探索的是：能不能在 Bitcoin L1 之上做出一套更复杂的资产和金融应用，而不是再复制一条 EVM 链。

现在还非常早，也非常实验性，但已经不只是停留在概念阶段，链上有真实的 mint、migration 和用户参与。

我自己已经实际跑过一遍整个参与流程，所以决定继续跟下去。

真正让我感兴趣的不是短期价格，而是接下来几个问题：

— CRC-20 能不能顺利完成完整的流转闭环
— Mint 结束后能不能形成真正的 Swap / LP 和流动性
— 会不会有更多钱包、Indexer、市场开始支持 CRC-20
— PRECOP 能不能从一次实验，继续长成 Bitcoin Native 的金融基础设施
— 如果生态真的起来，$LEAF 最终能捕获多少价值

目前 Mint 已经非常接近尾声。

但这里我要强调一下：我参与时和现在的市场条件已经不同，当前 legacy 流动性也比较薄。

所以这不是一条“现在赶紧冲”的 Call，也不建议因为看到这条就去追价格。

我更愿意把它当成一个 Early Alpha Research：

东西很早，赔率曾经很有意思，后面还有不少关键节点需要验证。

如果它最后没跑出来，这条就当一次早期实验记录。

如果以后真的从现在这个阶段一路长到更大的体量，我也会回来完整复盘——当时为什么关注、哪些判断对了、哪些判断错了。

Bitcoin Native 这种东西，真正有意思的往往就是在所有答案都还没出来的时候。

项目：
https://t.co/55Jy4fMubn

我会继续跟踪 CRC-20 / PRECOP，以及其他 Bitcoin Native 早期机会。

更多研究和 Alpha：
https://t.co/Z5GxfEJSw8

仅为个人研究记录，不是买入建议。

We are sharing an interim update regarding an exploit identified with @limitbreak Payment Processor V2, a NFT trading protocol maintained by the company Limit Break and which Magic Eden adopted to settle trades on EVM in 2024.

Magic Eden stopped using Payment Processor V2 in Oct 2024 and ceased our EVM marketplace altogether in Q1 2026. No live Magic Eden listings were impacted in this exploit. We will provide more updates as we investigate the impact further.

We are also contacting Limit Break as they are the owner & maintainer of the protocol to see what other mitigations can be done, including progress on pausing transfers on the protocol. Thank you to @0xQuit for the whitehat rescue and for bringing this to our collective attention: https://t.co/vXwUS5laJE

Why are ME listings being shown to be involved? 
NFTs listed on ME EVM from approx Feb 2024 to Oct 2024 could be impacted by this issue with the Limit Break Payment Processor v2 contract. Any listings on ME EVM after Oct 2024 should not be impacted here. We are still further refining our investigation and will provide more updates here.

In the meantime, if you listed or traded NFTs on Magic Eden’s EVM marketplace before we shut it down, revoke this contract:

Limit Break: Payment Processor (V2)

0x9A1D00bEd7CD04BCDA516d721A596eb22Aac6834

Go through our instructions here: https://t.co/34d0BQ6rh9
Ethereum → filter that address → revoke every NFT “approved for all” row

Base

See also 0xQuit’s tweet on revocation for further reference also: https://t.co/9guRvUZK1e

text:
CoinMarketCap 官方宣布已完成对加密衍生品数据平台 Coinglass 的收购，交易金额未披露。

表面看是一场数据平台的并购，深层却折射出 Web3 流量与基础设施的演进逻辑：  

1️⃣ 流量巨头的补短板之争
CMC（背靠币安）手握 1.15 亿 月活的超级散户入口，但在“杠杆、清算分布、期权”等专业衍生品数据上一直不如 Coinglass 精细。买下 Coinglass，直接用极低成本补齐了专业交易端的数据拼图。  

2️⃣ 衍生品战场的“流量前置”
牛熊交替中，现货行情只是基础，爆仓图、资金费率和未平仓量（OI）才是撮合交易、引导流动性的“真水龙头”。掌控了高级衍生品数据的展示权，就等于掌控了未来向交易所和衍生品协议导流的顶级入口。  

3️⃣ 独立工具的宿命
从区块链浏览器、行情软件到衍生品工具，独立数据平台的终局大概率要么靠高价 API 转型 ToB，要么被生态巨头收编为流量闭环的一环。Coinglass 保持独立运营，但商业变现和流量底座已经与超级巨头捆绑。  

数据终将向流量垄断者集中，下一个被并购的垂直数据工具会是谁？

Introducing Fluid Bench.

Fluid Bench is the new bit of TPN infrastructure that allows the subnet's pipeline to generate, review and score private versioned benchmarks.

It is a private benchmark built and run by TPN. We generate the questions ourselves across hundreds of topics, freeze them into a versioned epoch, and keep them private. Miners select it in TPN Bench like any other benchmark and get back a single score, without ever seeing the questions.

Differently from public benchmarks, Fluid Bench can't be studied, so the score reflects what the model can do, ultimately resulting in better model submissions through subnet competitions.

Production generation starts shortly, alongside competition 5 and TPN v0.2.

The "flippening" we didn't expect to arrive this early. 

Open weights are starting to look a lot like baseload power for AI.

They're not beating the best closed model outright atm. But they're close enough and good enough for the massive pile of work that doesn’t justify frontier pricing.

Then Astra, Opus, Fable etc become more like peaker plants: expensive capacity you pull in only when the task actually earns it.

If this keeps up, open weights could end up carrying most routine inference while closed labs make their money on the ugly tail of problems where failure is expensive.

Way more interesting outcome than “open eventually beats closed.”

Allocations begin today.

author: oskarth
quoted_text:
Another building block we use: chainfold

chainfold is a Rust library to deal with some of the inconveniences that come with handling on-chain events, especially reconciling after encountering a reorg.

Instead of forcing you to use a specific runtime, a storage backend, or an arbitrary "safe" block height that can be considered finalized, chainfold puts these batteries in your hands, that you can tune according to your specific usecase.

The design is simple enough: process an event, fold it into your local state, and when the block is finalized, persist the fold to storage, all while being able to roll back to a point that the data was known to be canonical.

We built this library to enable easier legacy system integration, where codebases cannot use modern languages / libraries that are well maintained, and the developers end up having to rebuild most of these components themselves.

More on the design, links and long-form writeup below 👇

text:
Solving agent identity with WebMCP

You gave your agent access to your account so it could buy something for you or book a dinner. Now your account is blocked. Is this the future of the agentic web?

One of the biggest problems with agents right now is giving them legitimate access to services on human behalf. 

More users are sending Muse, Instinct and other assistants into websites using their own credentials and authenticated browser sessions. The agent is acting on behalf of the user, but from the website's perspective it can look like a bad bot using a human account.

Resy, LinkedIn and others have already blocked user accounts because of this kind of automation ☠️

Web services are dealing with the question of how to give legitimate agents a dedicated path, and apply different permissions and limits to them. 

Luckily, WebMCP is spreading fast! WebMCP creates an interesting path to solve this as websites are starting to expose WebMCP tools specifically for agents. The website interface is now becoming:

Human lane - DOM, buttons, UI
Agent lane - WebMCP Tools 

So you effectively have an agent lane by just having WebMCP!

But having the dedicated agent lane doesn't mean "good" agents will use them, and also doesn't mean that "bad" agents will not try to cheat and use the human lane.

So there are few interesting questions to solve:
1) How do you give agents a reason to *actually use* the WebMCP agent lane instead of behaving like a human or calling the underlying APIs directly? 

agent developers might be afraid to get blocked, so easiest for them is just stick with the existing human path and not take the chance.

2) Once the agents use WebMCP agent lane regularly, how do you apply different policies to that traffic if WebMCP still talks to many of the same backend endpoints?

3) What do you do about bad agents that will pretend to be human? (problem old as the internet)

We wrote more about using WebMCP to solve this our in our new blog post:

https://t.co/pu2tMt3Q5X

If you want to test our alpha product for managing WebMCP sessions, fee free to shoot us a message: founders@nekuda.ai

author: taodotcom
quoted_text:
Introducing Fluid Bench.

Fluid Bench is the new bit of TPN infrastructure that allows the subnet's pipeline to generate, review and score private versioned benchmarks.

It is a private benchmark built and run by TPN. We generate the questions ourselves across hundreds of topics, freeze them into a versioned epoch, and keep them private. Miners select it in TPN Bench like any other benchmark and get back a single score, without ever seeing the questions.

Differently from public benchmarks, Fluid Bench can't be studied, so the score reflects what the model can do, ultimately resulting in better model submissions through subnet competitions.

Production generation starts shortly, alongside competition 5 and TPN v0.2.

Protocol risk curation looks like a clean software business until you pull open the distributor contracts.

We went through 11 live distributor integrations last week. Most curator businesses are not yet self-sustaining from vault fees alone.

The real numbers on the ground:

One retail integration charges 0% fees. The protocol is manually funding a 7% target yield out of pocket just to keep the shelf space.

Another takes 25% of APY, split 80/15/5 between exchange, curator, and middleware. The curator gets 15% of that 25% cut.

Base vault fees won't pay your team. Without offchain fee splits, custom wrappers, or protocol subsidies, the unit economics break. The business lives in the private distribution agreements, not the onchain fee switch.

text:
Jumper: The Super-App for Onchain Finance

Back in March 2023, when Jumper was incubated within LI.​FI, it was a completely different world.

We were just getting used to the reality of having many chains that people actually want to use - and user behaviour was changing in real time from being a chain maxi to just going wherever the best opportunities lie in crypto.

All of this required moving capital from one chain to another, and that’s where Jumper came in.

We started as a ‘bridge aggregation’ frontend, but even at launch a few years ago, it was never just about bridging. We offered users the best place for bridging across chains, but at the same time, we were aggregating DEXs and DEX aggregators to offer same-chain swaps.

And by combining the two actions, Jumper was one of the first apps to offer ‘cross-chain swaps’ - what has become industry standard today, and it was inevitable.

41 billion dollars in volume later, yes, bridging is still core to our business and a large chunk of our users trust Jumper with all their cross-chain activity today, and that trust has made Jumper the #1 app by bridging volume.

But our 100k monthly active users are not just using Jumper for bridging.

Beyond bridging, jumper is already one of the top 10 most widely used apps for swapping, with over $14 billion in swap volume.

In the past few years, we’ve made it our focus to expand our features and offering in the swapping market - a lot of this work recently went live in production with advanced trading features like limit orders, TWAPs and quote simulation.

Sounds standard, but look around and you’ll see there’s only a handful of teams who are able to do this across all the main blockchains in crypto.

And we’re now also the only app in crypto that is abstracting issuer and blockchain fragmentation from users for tokenized stocks with Jumper RWAs - again, nobody else is doing it, and there’s a reason why, it’s hard.

Building things in crypto is hard.
Building a product on one chain is complex.
Building a product like Jumper that touches 50+ chains is exponentially complex.

Our goal is to build an application that people can use across all of crypto with the same consistency and feature set that they get on apps on a single chain.

Beyond bridging and swapping, in the long term, we want users to use Jumper for all their onchain activity.

Users trust Jumper, they have used our products, and we believe they will continue using our products across categories as we bring the same aggregation expertise and abstract the UX across categories.

Jumper Earn is a testament to this thesis.

Launched in early 2026, the timing couldn’t have been worse. As we launched Earn, the industry was hit with the worst phase of hacks in DeFi - billions in capital were lost and billions more left onchain markets.

But as the markets are looking better and DeFi inflows are gaining momentum, Jumper Earn’s value of offering access to the best yield opportunities in crypto is resonating with users, and we’ve grown to 10M in attributed TVL in the last few weeks.

We will continue to ship and expand across categories. Jumper Perps is up next, and we’re super excited to bring perps with a twist to the market - this won’t be a vanilla integration. We’re going to offer access to multiple perps trading venues on Jumper - perps and aggregation with a simplified user experience, the Jumper way.

That’s a lot of products, and simply shipping them doesn’t guarantee anything. We’re well aware that even if we build the best products, it won’t lead to adoption.
And the super-app category is perhaps one of the most crowded ones in the industry.

But it is crowded for a reason - it is crowded because it’s a big market, and whoever does it right is going to build a massive company.

Our bet is that it will be Jumper.

Our goal is to build one place where people can access the best products and assets across the onchain economy, with the same consistency they’d expect from an app built on a single chain.

That’s the super-app thesis.

We know how to build products that work at scale.
We know how to simplify the UX of complicated tech that touches many chains.

But most importantly, we know and care about building distribution engines for growth more than anything else.

We’re not going to rest on our laurels and take our existing user base for granted - thinking that we can just sell new things to the same users. No, that’s not it.

With all our new products, our goal is to expand the user base and build new revenue lines for the growth of Jumper.

And when you bring it all under one roof - building the super-app for onchain finance.

It’s going to be hard, but anything worth doing is, and we’re up for the challenge.

The next chapter of Jumper is going to be fun.

Very excited for what comes next.

Make the Jump.

text:
Traditional search is just the Dewey Decimal System now.

A brilliant way to tell you where an answer lives. Less and less useful once something can simply hand you the answer. 

A few notes on the continued decline of search traffic to major US publishers:

Each era of discovery shrinks the gap between a question and its answer.

The card catalog pointed to a shelf. Google pointed to a page. 

The iPhone put Google in every pocket. Chatbots skip the pointing to just return the answer. 

US public library visits peaked in 2009, two years after the iPhone. They have roughly halved since.

Now look at the ramp. 

Google took 13 years to go from 1 billion searches a year to 1 trillion.

ChatGPT reached a ~900 billion prompt annual run rate in under three years.

The adoption curve for answers is far steeper than it ever was for search.

text: Recuerdo que cada año visitaba la tumba de Morazán en el cementerio de los ilustres y ahí la veía siempre descolorida, semi abandonada, sin asear. En silencio, siempre le prometía a su memoria que un día lograríamos hacer realidad su sueño, la reconsntrucción de la Federación Centroamericana, por la que él luchó y murió. Siempre le dejaba una modesta ofrenda floral y luego me retiraba, y me preguntaba: ¿Cómo era posible que un personaje del calibre de Francisco Morazán, cuyos restos yacían en suelo salvadoreño por su propia decisión (aunque nacido hondureño), no estuvieran en un mausoleo digno de su gran talla y representación histórica? Y les contaba esto a mis alumnos de la época y les narraba las historias y anécdotas de las guerras entre federalistas unionistas (que eran a la vez liberales) contra los conservadores y separatistas (financiados por los grandes terratenientes de las provincias centroamericanas, a quienes les convenía fragmentar el istmo, para sus propios, mezquinos, tozudos y primitivos intereses oligárquicos (quienes pasaron por mis aulas en esos años, lo recordarán muy  bien y pueden dar testimonio de mis palabras). Grande Francisco Morazán cuyos restos ahora yacen en un mausoleo digno de su legado para Centroamérica. Grande nuestro Presidente Nayib Bukele por reconocerlo y otorgárselo! quoted_text:
been thinking more on coherent messaging re: NEAR

let's ideate from first principles:

- the product of capitalism is markets

- capitalism -> markets -> competition -> specialization -> fragmentation

- within the specializations, there will be dominant leaders in each category

- SoV: gold, zec, btc

- trading: solana, hyperliquid, robinhood, binance

- currencies: usd, eur, gbp 

- and on it goes: ai inference, private compute, real estate, international stocks, metals, e-commerce yada yada

- this requires connective tissue, which has been traditionally served via something like binance

- but one centralized company can not serve this need for infinite markets. there are too many handicaps, lack of network effects, and singular points of risk and stoppage. this is a rare case of decentralization being necessary. neutrality is non-negotiable for unstoppable global trade.

- now, you may see where I'm going and say: well Ethereum and Cosmos already tried this. but that's wrong. what they tried to do was structurally flawed

- those models required the succeeding nodes (L2s and L3s) to be from within the ecosystem, but that is incoherent since i) you can't force success, ii) if one were to succeed, they would just want to own the platform

- the other model is of course the Solana/Hyperliquid model of having everything concentrated on the L1. this model works. however this requires a high-degree of specialization to be competitive. you won't out nasdaq solana. 

- but, NEAR does not need to do this. where there is concentration, there is also the need for connection.

- especially with their chain signature architecture, instead of forcing new internal nodes, they can just discover the successful ones and connect them to each other without ideology (see: NEAR intents supporting ZEC but also ZEC on Solana!)

- importantly, this is PvE and not zero sum. the more markets succeed, the more interesting NEAR becomes, i.e if Solana is one continent, and AI another, and Zcash another, then NEAR is the silk road.

so I think the coherent message for NEAR is: 

the market of markets — the capital of capital

text:
再给大家科普另一个业内常识。

一个交易所，做市商有两种，一种内部自己的做市商，一种外部合作做市商，

外部合作：
主流品牌有以下，Wintermute、GSR、Jump、DWF Labs、Keyrock 等（这是加密领域），或 Citadel、Virtu、Jane Street（这是传统金融）。

交易所与他们签订做市协议，给予激励，比如手续费返还、更低费率、有时还有授信或其他便利条件，cex 对他们的要求是同时要求是持续双边报价、维持一定点差深度、满足最小挂单量等。

内部/团队/关联做事：传统中相对少见。

交易所内部交易团队或自营部门直接挂单提供流动性，关联公司或子公司做市，这就是你为什么会看到二线所相互参股的直接原因。小型交易所为了快速上线交易对，自己先垫资金做市。

为什么有些交易所自己做市？本质是早期，或者实力不够，想更直接控制点差和盘口深度，自己赚点差。或者新币种刚上线、流动性极差时，外部做市商根本不愿意接。

为什么最后千叮咛万嘱咐不让你去垃圾所，因为大型正规交易所通常只做撮合和监管，自营有没有？有，但占比很少，垃圾所占比就大。

text:
MIT says 95% of company AI projects made zero dollars.

I read that twice.

Then I saw what the employees were doing behind their bosses' backs, and it made total sense.

When this report dropped, the internet already had its headline. AI is a bubble. The hype is over. Companies wasted billions on chatbots that don't work. AI stocks sold off the same week.

So I went and read what MIT actually counted.

They studied more than 300 public AI projects, interviewed people at 52 companies, and surveyed 153 senior leaders. Together, companies had poured $30 to $40 billion into AI.

95% of those projects showed zero impact on profit. Only about 5% of the custom tools companies built ever made it out of testing and into real daily work.

That part of the headline was true.

Then I kept reading, and the report flipped on me.

Only 40% of those companies had bought an official AI subscription for their staff. Workers at more than 90% of them were using AI every day anyway. Their own ChatGPT accounts. Their own Claude subscriptions. Paid for themselves, invisible to IT.

MIT calls it the shadow AI economy.

One story in the report explains the whole thing. A corporate lawyer's firm spent $50,000 on a special tool for analyzing contracts. She drafts in ChatGPT instead. The expensive tool spits out stiff summaries she can't change. ChatGPT lets her push back until the draft is right.

So the thing that failed was the $50,000 version. The $20 version was working the whole time.

The company tools mostly died for a boring reason. They can't learn. You correct them on Monday and they make the same mistake on Tuesday. And homemade tools did far worse than bought ones. Tools from outside specialists worked about two thirds of the time. Tools companies built themselves worked about a third of the time.

That was last summer. So I pulled this year's numbers, fully expecting companies to have fixed it by now.

They haven't.

In June, PagerDuty surveyed 1,250 office workers at companies making $500 million or more a year. Two out of three said they had used AI at work even though they believed their company didn't allow it. At companies with more than 1,500 employees, it hit 72%.

Deloitte's 2026 report shows companies finally started handing out official AI. The share of workers with approved tools jumped from under 40% to about 60% in one year. But among the people who got them, fewer than 60% use them in their daily work. Same as the year before.

Put those two side by side. Companies are finally paying for AI. Workers keep breaking the rules to use their own.

Now the fine print, because these numbers get abused in both directions.

MIT's report is preliminary, not peer-reviewed. It's built on interviews and surveys, not company earnings, and it measured results roughly six months after launch. Plenty of projects take longer than that to pay off. Zero profit impact doesn't mean zero value either. A tool can save your team ten hours a week without ever showing up on the earnings report. And PagerDuty sells software for managing exactly this problem, so they had a reason to go looking for it.

But strip all of that away and one thing survives.

Everyone shared this report as proof that AI doesn't work.

A year later, it reads like proof your employees figured AI out before your company did.

Borrowing USDC against Coinbase Tokenized Stocks is now possible on a dedicated @aave V4 instance on @base.

Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Spoke on @aave v4 lets users deposit stocks issued by @coinbase (AAPLc, AMZNc, GOOGLc, METAc, MSFTc, NVDAc, TSLAc) as collateral and borrow @circle USDC against them.

This allows users to keep their exposure to the stock without selling it while unlocking liquidity that can then be reinvested in other assets or spent, increasing capital efficiency.

Aave loans have no fixed term so users only need to keep a healthy LTV to avoid liquidation and they can repay the loan whenever they want.

In TradFi, borrowing against a stock portfolio means having access to a margin account that takes time and comes with account approvals, minimum balances requirements, and other broker terms

Aave v4 Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Instance reduces the complexity of this type of operation, opens access to more capital efficency, while leveraging onchain rails. At the same time, it brings more borrow demand for onchain assets that can pay a yield to users that want to provide liquidity to this market.

text:
you think the markets are really good at pricing in catalysts and you think it’s all “priced in”.

spoiler: it’s not, it’s inefficient. 

who do you think does the pricing in? us

how to turn Jev and Claude into a catalyst ranking cheat code for your coins:

1: Get a Jev API key
2: Save the key in a .env file in your project
3: Install TypeSafe's official skill in Claude Code so it knows how to call Jev correctly.
4: Ask Claude Code to set up a project (Python with a TypeSafe key, or TypeScript with a Vercel Gateway key) with separate files for your token watchlist, your Jev questions and your score thresholds.
5: Add a CLAUDE. md file saying that Jev only scores text, code handles all numbers and dates.
6: Have Claude Code build fetchers that collect governance proposals, project announcements, releases and unlock schedules for every token on your watchlist.
7: Convert every item into the same simple record: project, title, text, source link and event date.
8: Calculate how many days away each event is in code, because Jev cannot reliably compare dates.
9: Send each item to Jev in a single call that asks all your questions at once, which keeps it fast and cheap.
10: Ask Jev what type of catalyst it is, how much it could matter, how specific the timing is, and whether it is a recap or just hype.
11: Combine Jev's answers in code into one priority score, using weights you set and can change.
12: Route every item: drop non-catalysts, put unclear ones on a review list, and flag high-priority items and serious security incidents for a brief.
13: Have Claude read the full source for each flagged item and write a short brief.
14: Run it next to your normal research for a week and compare its picks with yours before you trust it.
15: Fix the questions or weights wherever it got things wrong, then test again.
16: Save the workflow as a Claude Skill and set up a scheduled task to run it once or twice a day.

start turning your knowledge into alpha asap.

The @CantonFdn is key to overseeing and maintaining the @CantonNetwork itself. However, the foundation itself is not one single beast...

Within the Foundation, exist several committees, made up of high calibre members, and with responsibilities over various areas of ecosystem operations.

They span everything from technological development, through to marketing and legal matters, but here are some of the most important...

Tokenomics Committee:
The Tokenomics Committee oversees one of the most crucial aspects of The Canton Network ecosystem - The economics and tokenomics of $CC. It effectively governs the economic parameters of Canton Coin. This means calibrating fee structures, determining traffic parameters, and even reviewing applications from potential Featured Apps.

Tech & Ops Committee: 
The Tech & Ops Committee oversees all the network's technological development, from directing architectural upgrades, through to tech-focused CIPs. It also evaluates and distributes builder grants and proposals from the Canton Development Fund.

Accountability Committee: 
As the name suggests, this committee is there to ensure accountability among ecosystem participants like Super Validators and Featured Apps. It ensures milestones are hit, while even suggesting remediation action for underperformance.

This is really just a taste. 

As the Canton ecosystem grows and matures, so too does the Canton Foundation's committee system. 

There are even various subcommittees, such as the Collateral Subcommittee, recently joined by @Cashen_cc and whose purpose is to design and govern the protocols that allow financial institutions to undertake tokenised collateral across the Canton Network.

但有一条信息我觉得很多人忽略了：

@BlackRock 最近直接把 AI Agent + Stablecoin Payment 放到一起讲，Block 也刚加入 x402 Foundation，把 Bitcoin Lightning 接进 x402 

原本更像 @Base 自己在推的东西，现在开始往 @Solana、#Bitcoin 和更多网络扩。

上次看 x402 的时候，还是一堆小票刚冒头。今天再看， solana:PAYmo6moDF3Ro3X6bU2jwe2UdBnBhv8YjLgL1j4DxGu 又走强了不少

我的理解也很简单：

text:
I often see early-stage founders make two types of mistakes in their pitch decks: 

1. one is ignoring competitors - pretending they don't exist and failing to be candid when investors ask about them

2. the other is disparaging competitors - deliberately downplaying their strengths to make themselves look better. 

From an investor's perspective, however, both approaches signal immaturity.

What I look for are founders who acknowledge the strength of their competition yet remain confident in their ability to launch a even better product and outperform them. 

An objective, comprehensive, and insightful analysis of competitors demonstrates a clear understanding of the competitive landscape, which instills confidence in investors rather than raising doubts.

🔥LATEST: Strategy wants to start paying DIVIDENDS DAILY on four of its preferred stocks.

The board approved putting proposed changes for $STRF, $STRC, $STRK and $STRD to a shareholder vote on October 28.

If approved:
- Every calendar day becomes a dividend record date
- Declared dividends are paid the next business day

Dividend rates and total regular dividend obligations stay unchanged

$STRC could begin daily payouts on November 2, 2026, while $STRF, $STRK and $STRD could follow from January 4, 2027.

For holders, the key benefit is better cash-flow timing and potentially stronger appeal to income-focused investors.

But this does NOT increase the dividend itself. 

It changes how frequently investors get paid, not how much they receive.

Of note, Holders of $STRC, $STRD, $STRF and $STRK do NOT vote on the proposal.

If approved by the eligible voting stockholders, the changes would take effect after Strategy files the amended certificates of designation in Delaware.

text:
Binance-Owned CoinMarketCap Acquires Crypto Derivatives Data Platform CoinGlass

CoinMarketCap has completed its acquisition of crypto derivatives data platform CoinGlass for an undisclosed amount. CoinMarketCap said it will integrate CoinGlass data including open interest, funding rates, liquidations and options into its broader market-data offering. CoinGlass covers 28 exchanges and more than 2,500 instruments, has over 5 million monthly users and more than 10,000 API clients, while CoinMarketCap says it serves about 115 million monthly users. CoinGlass will continue operating independently under its existing brand, with its website, app, free tools, APIs and pricing unchanged for now.

CoinMarketCap itself was acquired by Binance in 2020. The purchase price was not officially disclosed, though The Block reported at the time that the deal could be worth as much as $400 million. Subsequent reporting said the transaction was structured primarily in equity and BNB.

Just finished accumulating a bigger solana:KMNo3nJsBXfcpJTVhZcXLW7RmTwTt4GVFE7suUBo9sS position on the open market.

Very bullish on the overall trend of tokenized equities, and I genuinely believe the supply here grows another 100x from here, led by @solana.

I've been thinking a lot about how to best position for this. I'm a big fan of what Backpack, Securitize and co are doing, but I'm still hesitant on the business model and monetizability of the issuers, especially at these valuations.

Much more interesting to me are the businesses and protocols actually built on top of that layer, the ones that benefit massively from this secular trend.

DEXs are the obvious play here, but what has excited me far more is @kamino.

I'm usually not overly excited about lending businesses, but they made the move into tokenized equity lending early and have been dominating market share ever since. As I expect this market to grow orders of magnitude from here, there's a realistic path for Kamino to massively expand their business in a positive-sum way, and a real shot at rivaling Morpho. Especially since I expect tokenized equities to keep being led by Solana, which Kamino has already proven it can dominate.

Beyond that, the recent hire of @WeiszM is massive, and in my opinion still overlooked. If you want to dominate the upcoming institutional adoption and the influx of trillions in capital as an onchain financial business, you need someone at the top who not only speaks the TradFi language, but has the background and network to actually get the right things moving and open the right doors.

Let's see how this evolves, but definitely one of the more interestingly positioned DeFi protocols right ahead of a massive DeFi supercycle.

author: Bookof_Eth
quoted_text:
This is Ethereum.

There are 291 projects, companies, protocols and communities in this image. It is still only a fraction of what has been built.

What makes this remarkable isn't just the scale. It's how that scale was created.

There is no parent company behind all of this. No CEO allocating capital across these projects, no central entity deciding who gets to build or what the ecosystem should become. Thousands of independent teams, communities and individuals have built their own piece of Ethereum, often with completely different goals, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

Finance, credit, stablecoins, payments, RWAs, privacy, identity, gaming, social applications, infrastructure, culture and public goods are increasingly becoming parts of the same composable economy.

That structure matters.

Value isn't concentrated in one company at the top. It is distributed across protocols, builders, users, communities and assets. Yet they can still reinforce each other because they share Ethereum as common infrastructure.

And underneath that economy sits ethereum:native.

ethereum:native  secures Ethereum, pays for its blockspace and is used throughout the ecosystem as collateral, liquidity and money. As more applications, assets and economic activity settle on Ethereum, the economic role of ETH grows with it.

This is why we believe ETH remains heavily undervalued.

The market often looks at ETH as another crypto asset. We look at what is actually being built around it.

291 logos in one image, with many more still missing. And most of the world's people, assets and economic activity haven't even moved onchain yet. 

Ethereum is no longer just an experiment in decentralized technology.

It is becoming an entire economy,  built by many, owned by no one, with ETH at its core.

BOOElieve in the future of Ethereum and ethereum:native

Borrowing USDC against Coinbase Tokenized Stocks is now possible on a dedicated @aave V4 instance on @base.

Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Spoke on @aave v4 lets users deposit stocks issued by @coinbase (AAPLc, AMZNc, GOOGLc, METAc, MSFTc, NVDAc, TSLAc) as collateral and borrow @circle USDC against them.

This allows users to keep their exposure to the stock without selling it while unlocking liquidity that can then be reinvested in other assets or spent, increasing capital efficiency.

Aave loans have no fixed term so users only need to keep a healthy LTV to avoid liquidation and they can repay the loan whenever they want.

In TradFi, borrowing against a stock portfolio means having access to a margin account that takes time and comes with account approvals, minimum balances requirements, and other broker terms

Aave v4 Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Instance reduces the complexity of this type of operation, opens access to more capital efficency, while leveraging onchain rails. At the same time, it brings more borrow demand for onchain assets that can pay a yield to users that want to provide liquidity to this market.

text:
#AurorAI is officially underway after the international consortium's successful kickoff. 

The mission: give Europe an AI toolkit that's ready before the next outbreak, not after it. 

Its data backbone: the OriginTrail Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG). 

14 partners. 10 countries. One platform. 

@AURORAI_project unites research institutes and universities, public health authorities, healthcare providers and technology companies. 

The platform will be put to the test at national and local level, and the public health partners show the scale: from Turkey's Ministry of Health, covering a country of 86 million people, to Belgium's national public health institute and a regional hospital network in Catalonia. 

At the kickoff, @DrevZiga, co-founder of OriginTrail, walked the consortium through how the DKG keeps every partner's data verifiable, sovereign and AI-ready. 

How it works: 
→ Ownership. Health and research data becomes Knowledge Assets on the DKG, each with a Uniform Asset Locator (UAL): blockchain-backed proof of who published it and that it hasn't been tampered with. 
→ Sovereignty. Context graphs control which regions see which metadata. The data itself stays where it is. 
→ Verification. Partners submit data proofs through DKG nodes and check authenticity on-chain, instantly. → Interoperability. Shared ontologies and data standards make data from different countries and institutions work together. 

Then the AI agents get to work. That verified layer is the first input to AURORAI's decision support system, alongside pathogen models and population and mobility simulations. 

The result: policy guidance for ministries of health, and coordinated clinical and scientific guidance for healthcare providers and authorities. 

Every recommendation traces back to a verifiable source.

text:
Every on-chain finance app is racing to become the one you never leave

What used to be a clear division of labor where wallets hold assets, DEXs swap them, bridges move them across chains, is collapsing into a single fight for the same real estate: the one interface a user opens every day for everything

@binance, @coinbase & @JupiterExchange are chasing it from the CEX & DEX side whereas @MetaMask & @phantom from the wallet side

Each stacks features that used to belong to separate categories: perps, RWAs, yield, cards, social feeds, all converging into one app

We ran a detailed comparison benchmarking the key superapp features across the category, Jumper @jumperapp included as the newest entrant and because they seem to be having their TGE soon

Where Jumper Started
• Built its name as a bridge aggregator, achieving #1 by bridging volume and ~15% market share
• 100,000 monthly active users, and a top 10 position among aggregators by swap volume

- - - - -

Superapp Features: Highlights
• RWA aggregation: Jupiter, MetaMask, and Phantom each plug into one tokenized-stock provider, mostly @Ondo Global Markets. Jumper pulls from six issuers at once: Ondo, @xStocksFi, @RobinhoodApp, @Backpack, Coinbase, bStocks → Jumper’s POV focuses on being issuer-agnostic, similar to its bridge aggregation strategy
• Yield: One-click transaction zap across 120+ vaults and 20+ protocols, plus a Dust Sweeper cleaning up small balances most apps don't bother with
• Advanced trading tools: Live features include pre-sign transaction simulation, smart slippage, and auto order-splitting above a size threshold

Where Gaps Exist
• No native discovery feed for memecoins yet, where Jupiter has AlphaScan and Phantom acquired @solsniperxyz 
• Perps aggregation hasn't launched, still pending with its own token and USD incentives via Ondo, while Jupiter, MetaMask, and Phantom already have live perps rails
• No card or neobank product, an area every other app in this comparison has already shipped an MVP minimally

- - - - - 
Closing Thoughts
The category is consolidating fast, and the apps winning aren't necessarily the ones with the most features. There is no one clear winner yet, just some leaders leading in certain features

Teams who continue to abstract away complexity while still giving power users the tools they actually want will continue to extend their lead. That being said, Jumper's bet is chain-abstraction and asset-coverage first, followed everything else after 

The gaps in distribution and consumer-facing products (cards, mini-apps, discovery) are where the wallets and CEXes have a head start. For now, very few competitors are issuer-agnostic on RWAs + more Superapp-like features coming soon (inc. Perps)

text:
There used to be a magazine for almost every weird corner of business. Commercial refrigeration had one. So did the people running regional self-storage, and somebody genuinely waited on it every month, to the point their spouse couldn't understand why they cared this much about a trade magazine.

Then most of them got bought, squeezed for the subscriber list and the events money, and that was that. Social took over after and dumped everyone into one big feed, and the specific insight you used to get about your own small world sort of dissolved into it.

We've been rebuilding that feeling for years now. A few thousand people who spend their 9-to-5 the way you do, in a room that's actually theirs.

And the part I care about most is the part that got the magazines killed. We built this one so it can't get sold off and hollowed out the second it's worth something.

Binance-Owned CoinMarketCap Acquires Crypto Derivatives Data Platform CoinGlass

CoinMarketCap has completed its acquisition of crypto derivatives data platform CoinGlass for an undisclosed amount. CoinMarketCap said it will integrate CoinGlass data including open interest, funding rates, liquidations and options into its broader market-data offering. CoinGlass covers 28 exchanges and more than 2,500 instruments, has over 5 million monthly users and more than 10,000 API clients, while CoinMarketCap says it serves about 115 million monthly users. CoinGlass will continue operating independently under its existing brand, with its website, app, free tools, APIs and pricing unchanged for now.

CoinMarketCap itself was acquired by Binance in 2020. The purchase price was not officially disclosed, though The Block reported at the time that the deal could be worth as much as $400 million. Subsequent reporting said the transaction was structured primarily in equity and BNB.

Borrowing USDC against Coinbase Tokenized Stocks is now possible on a dedicated @aave V4 instance on @base.

Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Spoke on @aave v4 lets users deposit stocks issued by @coinbase (AAPLc, AMZNc, GOOGLc, METAc, MSFTc, NVDAc, TSLAc) as collateral and borrow @circle USDC against them.

This allows users to keep their exposure to the stock without selling it while unlocking liquidity that can then be reinvested in other assets or spent, increasing capital efficiency.

Aave loans have no fixed term so users only need to keep a healthy LTV to avoid liquidation and they can repay the loan whenever they want.

In TradFi, borrowing against a stock portfolio means having access to a margin account that takes time and comes with account approvals, minimum balances requirements, and other broker terms

Aave v4 Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Instance reduces the complexity of this type of operation, opens access to more capital efficency, while leveraging onchain rails. At the same time, it brings more borrow demand for onchain assets that can pay a yield to users that want to provide liquidity to this market.

text:
AI 都快把大学教育打成夕阳产业了，有个人今年 31 岁，已经读了 12 个顶级大学学位，而且还没准备停。

《纽约时报》最近写了一个故事。

主人公 Jamie Beaton，Harvard 本科，之后一路读 Stanford、Yale、Oxford、Princeton、Cornell、Dartmouth、清华、Columbia，现在又跑去 Brown 读数据科学。

正常人的 LinkedIn 学历栏是简历，他那个已经有点像滚动字幕了。

更离谱的是，他还不是那种什么都不干、专门靠读书刷成就的职业学生。

Jamie 十几岁的时候就在新西兰研究怎么申请美国名校，高中毕业拿了 Harvard、Yale、Princeton 等 25 所大学的 offer。进 Harvard 前，他已经开始做 Crimson Education，后来一边上学，一边把这家公司做到了超过 6 亿美元估值。

他在 Harvard 时加了 15 个学生组织，凌晨两点还在处理公司电话；大二自己给 Tiger Management 创始人 Julian Robertson 发邮件，后来每周两天从波士顿跑纽约工作，Tiger 最后还投了 Crimson。

后来到了 Columbia，又出现了一个很好笑的场景。

老师开学以后发现 Jamie 怎么一直不来上课，一问才知道，他人还在新西兰，因为把课表搞错了。

他当时正在奥克兰大学给别人上创业课。

过几天飞回纽约继续当学生，作业一份没落，电脑上同时开着工作邮件和股票账户，最后还顺手在班里认识了现在的老婆。

他老师 Amy Chua 对他的评价特别准确：

「他就是停不下来申请东西。」

Jamie 自己倒不觉得这有什么奇怪。

前几个学位，他说是为了补具体能力，后面越来越像兴趣驱动。今天在 Princeton 学量化金融，明天就能拿公司里试；白天经营一家几亿美元的公司，晚上继续回学校交作业。

这也是我觉得这个故事在 2026 年特别有意思的地方。

这两年大家天天讨论 AI 会不会把大学干掉，知识越来越便宜，课程越来越不值钱，甚至一个顶级教授讲半年才能教完的东西，以后一个 Agent 几小时就能帮你搭完整套学习路径。

Jamie 偏偏走到了另一个极端。

当获取知识越来越不需要学校，他却把学校读成了一种基础设施。

他要的可能早就不只是那张文凭了。

教授、同学、研究环境、跨学科的训练，以及强迫自己在一个陌生领域重新当学生，这些东西暂时还没那么容易被一个聊天框完全替掉。

当然，这里面也有一个很讽刺的地方。

Jamie 自己经营的 Crimson，卖的恰恰就是一套高度工业化的精英教育路线，怎么规划、怎么选学校、怎么把一个十几岁的孩子送进 Ivy League。有人愿意为这套服务花几十万美元。

一边是 AI 在把知识的价格疯狂往下打。

另一边，最顶级的教育 credential、筛选和圈层，价格还在继续往上走。

AI 可能会让学东西越来越便宜，但被谁承认你学过东西，目前看一点都没有变便宜。

Jamie 读到第 12 个学位，知识正在变得免费。

名校还没有。

这只鸡吃的是 USDC，下的蛋是一套经过筛选的代币化 RWA 收益，再叠一层杠杆，目标净收益往 10% 以上走。底层饲料目前就三样： @humafinance 的 $PST 是做跨境支付融资、 @USDai_Official 的 $sUSDai 做 AI GPU 贷款、 @HastraFi   的 ethereum:0x19ebb35279a16207ec4ba82799cc64715065f7f6 做优质住宅净值抵押债权。

单吃这三样，蛋大概是 5%–6% 那个量级，但是杠杆一加上，蛋变大，风险也跟着变大。

组织上各管一段，Bitwise 当饲养员，跟着市场变化设计资产配置、借贷和风险参数，既要产量，也要信用质量和流动性； @EmberProtocol 管鸡舍，金库运营、所有交易落地都由它执行；Yield Network 和 y10k Capital 则是流动性联合体和基石流动性提供方，先把水池垫上。只要过得了 Bitwise 的尽调标准和风险框架，这只鸡以后还能换更多种类的 RWA 饲料。

这样讲讲就明白了吧？PPLUS 一开现在 TVL 已经干到 $12.84M 了，30D APY 在 11.52%，Vault 部署在 Sui 跟 ETH 上，这个数据全链都是有竞争力的，毕竟，它的策展人是 Bitwise 啊！

就这还没有玩花活儿哦，你完全可以继续把 PPLUS 放到借贷平台玩 DeFi 乐高，套利、循坏贷都玩起来啊。

我挪一点过来生点🥚补补，营养不够了。

Just finished accumulating a bigger solana:KMNo3nJsBXfcpJTVhZcXLW7RmTwTt4GVFE7suUBo9sS position on the open market.

Very bullish on the overall trend of tokenized equities, and I genuinely believe the supply here grows another 100x from here, led by @solana.

I've been thinking a lot about how to best position for this. I'm a big fan of what Backpack, Securitize and co are doing, but I'm still hesitant on the business model and monetizability of the issuers, especially at these valuations.

Much more interesting to me are the businesses and protocols actually built on top of that layer, the ones that benefit massively from this secular trend.

DEXs are the obvious play here, but what has excited me far more is @kamino.

I'm usually not overly excited about lending businesses, but they made the move into tokenized equity lending early and have been dominating market share ever since. As I expect this market to grow orders of magnitude from here, there's a realistic path for Kamino to massively expand their business in a positive-sum way, and a real shot at rivaling Morpho. Especially since I expect tokenized equities to keep being led by Solana, which Kamino has already proven it can dominate.

Beyond that, the recent hire of @WeiszM is massive, and in my opinion still overlooked. If you want to dominate the upcoming institutional adoption and the influx of trillions in capital as an onchain financial business, you need someone at the top who not only speaks the TradFi language, but has the background and network to actually get the right things moving and open the right doors.

Let's see how this evolves, but definitely one of the more interestingly positioned DeFi protocols right ahead of a massive DeFi supercycle.

The new Copilot is Microsoft’s bet that the AI race is moving from models to products. 

It doesn’t need to own the best model if Copilot can choose among them and keep the customer inside Microsoft.

The potential secret weapon is Autopilot (what I’ve been calling Muse for Business). It knows your workflows, sits across the apps and data you already use, and keeps working even when you step away.

It’s a preview of the battle to come in enterprise AI. OpenAI and Anthropic are racing from models into products. Can they build their own version of this? And can they match Microsoft on the boring-but-critical stuff: permissions, identity, auditability and control, as agents become more autonomous?

My full conversation with @satyanadella. We also talk open vs. closed models, US-China Summit, regulation and the infrastructure buildout.

text: Today we are announcing an AI-assisted breakthrough in Ethereum development.
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
One step closer to 4-8x faster Ethereum finality!

It took some time and lots of tokens, but we now have a formally verified proposal for a decoupled consensus protocol in I* (a future Ethereum upgrade)! Not yet a full spec (up next), but it includes all the key consensus-relevant details to become one.

Since Ethereum aspires to be live without most of the stake online, the protocol involves many more components than a normal BFT protocol, and its correctness involves much more than standard safety and liveness. Those nuanced properties are now verified!

What's more, I came away convinced that all protocol design will involve AI-assisted Formal Verification in the future, both for correctness and iteration speed.

The work wasn't limited to just:

Design the protocol -> Formally verify it

Instead, the loop became more like:

Design -> Formal Model -> Find exactly what breaks and why -> Redesign it.

For a fairly complicated protocol like this one, I think having the Lean model be part of the design loop played a big role in accelerating the process.

A future with agents paired with formal models is a superpower for Ethereum development, because they can then use those models to find exactly where an argument breaks down, formalize counterexamples, test proposed fixes, iterate on the protocol.

Many details that would slip under the radar when asking agents (and indeed, humans) can now be specified exactly and checked by the Lean kernel. This then forces agents to be more precise and lets them make verifiable progress on their own. It's been incredible to see this play out, seeing agents find gaps and propose protocol changes to fix them.

In other words, autoresearch can speed up protocol design, formal verification is here to stay, and Ethereum Finality will get faster.

text:
Announcing Cosign.

Silicon Valley knows people by watching other people know them. One person's visible belief becomes a signal to someone else, and the network updates its priors.

Ascendancy is a game of two moves: self-made wins and high-status vouches. The earlier someone is in their trajectory, the less proof there is to go on, and the more meaningful the vouch. Belief compounds.

People used to earn status through rites of passage like graduating college and landing prestigious jobs. People collect status in bits now, 24/7, often outside any formal system. Showing your work in public has become the new warm intro.

Vouches take many forms. A tweet, an invite, an introduction, an angel check. Being undeniable and getting credible people to say so is how you become somebody in Silicon Valley.

The game only works if new people can win. Everyone benefits when good people get pulled into the game faster.

If you believe in someone early, say so.

Two years after the airdrop, Hyperliquid has cleared $5.4T of perps volume, holds 57% of decentralised perp open interest and has routed $1.28B of revenue into buybacks.

It was never pitched as the best perp DEX though. It was pitched as the house of all finance.

In our most recent report by @zerokn0wledge_, we walk through that house room by room:

- Native perps: an $18B open interest record, 49% of Binance's book, and no publicly announced incentive programme since 2024.

- HIP-3: $611B in under a year, a category of onchain RWA perps that Hyperliquid created, 98% of it in one franchisee's hands.

- The empty rooms: HIP-4 at 0.1% of prediction markets, spot at 2% of Binance, HyperEVM at 1.5% of revenue, and why the stellar perp product itself is the biggest reason for the lagging adoption.

- Washington: why regulation is key, featuring a perps-as-futures order, a CME lawsuit against it, and Kraken's parent company Payward looking to deploy Hyperliquid HIP-3* markets for US clients through its own clearinghouse.

- The 411M HYPE community reserve, what has actually left it since genesis, and why we think the airdrop odds might be mispriced.

Full report below.

text:
While I deeply respect the cryptographic research that @nemothenoone and the @allocinitxyz team are pursuing to enable covenants on Bitcoin without a soft fork, it’s worth emphasizing that the cryptography underlying this approach is still highly experimental, and its security assumptions are far from established.

It will likely take years of research and scrutiny before there is enough confidence in these constructions for use in Bitcoin applications — and realistically, that confidence may never materialize.

I love the boldness of their vision and I’m impressed by the progress so far. At the same time, I think it’s important that the community has a clear understanding of where the research currently stands and how uncertain its practical viability remains from a cryptographic perspective.

text:
前几天正好在 @EthereumSH 场外和朋友聊到过这个问题。

当时我就在推销自己的暴论——抗审查和隐私几乎不是一个技术问题：https://t.co/my7TyOBC6y

今天的世界上有两个对抗性特别强的样本。第一当然是朝鲜黑客，第二是中东恐怖主义。他们大多数时候基本只推荐捐赠 BTC、XMR 和 ETH。（下图片来源 @trmlabs

Zcash 完全不纳入考虑，明文 ZEC Transaction 几乎没有利用价值（可能比 Dogecoin 还不如，而 Shielded ZEC Transaction 在实践上几乎和  TornadoCash 里面出来的钱一样都会被主流交易所拒绝。

说比 Dogecoin 还不如原因是 Zcash 矿工网络多元化极差。美国政府曾一度要求各大比特币矿池拒绝将中东恐怖组织的 transaction 纳入比特币区块，一度造成部分交易长时间无法上链。Zcash 必然完全无法承受同等级别的 PoW 层审查攻击。

Zcash 案例中 viaBTC/Foundry/鱼池等五大矿工打包了 90%的区块，鱼池和 Foundry 应该都有拒绝打包特定交易的历史。
说夸张点，黑客行动如果较慢，协调回滚/分叉都有可能。

而 Monero/ETH/BTC 广泛的家庭矿工/独立矿工群体可以确保交易至少迟早会被确认。

况且经常洗钱的朋友们都知道这个工作的重点不是本身技术流有多优雅，而是有多少合法合规交易在为灰色黑色流量打掩护。
在 Monero 案例中本质上是强制要求所有使用者都共享分风险，互相掩护。但 Zcash 里却允许合法流量走明文，本质上灰色/黑色流量几乎完全没受任何掩护。
Zcash 的成功是叙事龙头地位捕获的成功，而非隐私和抗审查的成功。

最后 ETH、BTC 虽然是纯粹明文，但毕竟出口繁杂，有各种 OTC、跨链、DEX、伊朗/俄罗斯自己的非合作交易所等等可以利用。操作空间够足，本身被回滚、被分叉风险又足够低。
而被回滚、被分叉风险足够低是建立在矿工群体多元性的基础上的。

我自己是（或曾是）以太坊和门罗币家庭矿工。Be a good champ, run a node or begin your solo staking.
author: lurenbian
quoted_text:
既然ZEC是隐私币，为什么每次黑客都还是会把资金转换成ETH？昨天在Bitget被盗后很多朋友都提出了这个问题，确实几乎所有能历数的大型黑客事件，被盗的稳定币、山寨币都会被快速转成ETH，其实原因非常简单，顺着我的逻辑往下看
1.对于黑客来说，相比于隐私，安全更重要，一定要确保自己辛辛苦苦盗走的钱不会被冻结，而绝大多数稳定币、山寨币都有黑名单，大部分公链也都可以节点回滚，所以黑客必须第一时间快速把盗走的资金转换为不可被冻结的资产。
2.这时候你会问，那BTC也不会被回滚，更没有黑名单，为什么不换成BTC呢？答案是当然会换，但是要慢慢换，因为黑客在链上和交易所里盗走的绝大多数资产都是在以太坊主网上的，当然是直接换成ETH速度最快，不需要等着跨链，这时候必须要拼手速，否则慢悠悠的等跨完早都被冻结了，所以ZEC等其他的隐私币也是同样的道理。
3.刚才说到相比于隐私，安全更重要，所以快速换成ETH确保安全后，黑客才会高枕无忧，接下来十几天甚至几个月，慢悠悠的把ETH拆成几千上万个地址，然后用THORChain这些洗币桥和混币器慢慢的换成BTC。
4.然后经过长达几年的时间，大量小额分批掉通过场外和地下钱庄把BTC兑现。
所以隐私不隐私的，黑客根本不在意的好伐，人家有太多手段把钱洗出去。
当然黑客喜欢用ETH的原因还有一个，就是人家朝鲜是真的办过平壤以太坊大会啊🤣

text:
I manifested @jonwu_ into my life, and I did four very specific things to make it happen: 

1. I stopped consuming all man-hating content. Jokes count. I realized I would say "I don't hate men" but my TikTok would tell a different story. I had been down a bad rabbit hole after a breakup. You are what you consume. I deleted TikTok and never looked back. 

2. I re-programmed my energy to be open to men. Instead of having closed off energy to potential suitors, I just told myself, I am open, I am open, I am open. It made dating way more fun and stopped me from judging books by their covers right away. 

3. I stopped believing I was in lack of love. This was very important. I used to be so sad about being single. Then one day I woke up, and I decided to list out all of the ways I had love in my life -- my family, my friends, myself -- my whole life was romantic. And how could I be without love if I am love. I stopped going to bed upset, I lived with an energetic, playful and loving energy that was truly oozing from me inner to my outer self. 

4. I wrote down 80 words in a notebook about the type of man I wanted to call into my life. My list had 0 attributes, as in I did not write about his wealth, his interests, his height, what he looked like. Instead I focused on qualities: kindness, generosity, deep, loyal, funny. Literally I filled a whole page of qualities only, tore it out of my notebook and put it in the Little Prince. 

The day after I wrote the 80 qualities on a page, I was talking to Jon Wu about Joshua tree. I felt a calm voice tell me from my inner world that he was the one. 

I had never had such clarity about a man in my life. The rest is history. 

Words are magic, energy amplifies it. You want love, be love.
